title: 1. [Home](https://uidai.gov.in/en)
section: 2. When I link my bank accounts, shares, mutual funds and my mobile phones with Aadhaar, will UIDAI not get this information?
text:
### 
2. When I link my bank accounts, shares, mutual funds and my mobile phones with Aadhaar, will UIDAI not get this information?

  * 
Absolutely not. When you give your Aadhaar number to banks, mutual fund companies, and mobile phone companies, they only send your Aadhaar number along with your encrypted biometrics or OTP (given for authentication), or demographic details like your name, etc., to UIDAI for authentication of your identity. No account details are shared with UIDAI.

As far as UIDAI is concerned, it responds to such authentication requests by replying either ‘Yes’ or ‘No’.
* 
In case of an e-KYC request by the requesting entity, if the authentication response is ‘Yes’, your basic KYC details (name, address, photo, etc.) available with UIDAI, are also sent to the requesting entity. UIDAI will never receive or collect the details of your bank, investments, insurance, etc.

### 

  * 
Absolutely false. Just as by merely knowing your ATM card number, no one can withdraw money from the ATM machine; by knowing your Aadhaar number alone, no one can hack into your bank account and withdraw money.
  * 
Your bank account is safe if you don’t part with your PIN/OTP given by banks.
  * 
Rest assured, there has not been a single case of financial loss due to Aadhaar. Aadhaar number alone cannot be used for banking or any other service.
